text:
micah: quick heads-up — overnight reprocesses (EU agg pipeline) spiked and triggered the new tenant-throttle path, causing a bunch of small tenants to get starved. noticed ~40% of replay jobs went to LOW_PRIORITY lane and then timed out. :eyes:
anya: ugh. do you have the shard ids / example tenant ids?
micah: yep, repro list attached in logs. seems correlated with many tiny windows replays from 02:00–03:30 UTC. shard 112 and 117 were hot.
omar: are we sure this is a routing policy bug vs quota exhaustion? the throttle logic should only move tasks when slot pressure > 0.8.
jess: I looked at console traces — requests were routed to the aggressive fallback lane before the quota delta was computed. looks like quota-check RPC returned stale values (cache TTL 5s).
tim: that TTL is intentional for perf. but if quota RPC is occasionally 500-ing, fallback should not preemptively demote. we need a jittered retry backoff.
michael (ops-bot): deploy 5378010000: rolled back routing change 5378008000 to mitigate immediate regressions.
micah: rollback helped recover throughput but we still have a backlog. long-term we should improve routing decision to a two-step: 1) optimistic route, 2) verify quota, else graceful bump.
anya: agree. also proposal: add a "dry-run" flag in Console when scheduling a reprocess so customers can see estimated slot consumption and fallback probability. UX would show a risk score.
omar: dry-run is good, but we need it to simulate prefix/KV cache warmness — many failures were due to cold KV lookups amplifying slot usage. dry-run should accept a cache-hit profile override.
jess: for telemetry team it'll be useful to see estimated token cost and predicted latency percentiles. can we piggyback on the existing estimator endpoint? (`/v1/estimate/replay`)
tim: estimator endpoint currently uses historical hit rates. add an override query param `cache_profile=cold|warm|observed`. default remains observed.
micah: for immediate triage I ran a targeted backfill with a smaller batch size and forced warm-cache replays; that cleared ~60% of the small-tenant backlog. command I used:```bash
python -m replayer --shard=112 --start=2026-03-01T02:00Z --end=2026-03-01T04:00Z --batch-size=64 --force-warm-cache
```
anya: nice. can you paste the logs for the warm run (latency p95/p99)?
micah: p95 dropped from 1.2s to 0.45s, p99 from 3.6s to 0.9s. KV lookups were the main delta.
ops-bot: alert: replay-queue-depth > 1000 (resolved after rollback)
jess: follow-ups: (1) add cache_profile to estimator and CLI, (2) console dry-run with risk score and estimated slots, (3) make routing fallback wait for quota-check success with 200ms max wait + jittered retry, (4) add an operator-only throttle bypass for urgent small-tenant cleanups.
omar: for (4) I'd prefer a scoped lease token (single-use) rather than bypass flag — safer for auditing.
tim: agree with scoped lease token approach. implement as `replay_lease=<lease-id>` which the console can mint with expiry and tenant scope.
anya: timeline? this can be a small project: estimator change + CLI + console flag + routing tweak. target next sprint for the first two.
micah: I'll open a PR for the estimator changes and the `--force-warm-cache` CLI flag (small patch). tagging @anya for the Console UX mockups.
anya: I'll sketch the dry-run card and add a toggle for "Simulate cache cold/warm" + risk score color. will post mock by EOD.
jess: also adding a telemetry alert: if routing fallback rate > 5% for > 10m, auto-escalate to SRE channel.
ops-bot: runbook reminder: if backlog > 5000 and fallback-rate > 10% escalate to oncall.
micah: thanks — will follow up with logs + PR link. :thumbsup:
